commands.disposition: Mutation baseline fixture could not resolve its copied runner path; this attempt does not demonstrate a killed mutant. Later corrected mutation receipts remain separate.

Old code refused the valid policy-marker projection and failed five dispatch/schema binding assertions; one reported error is retained, not relabeled as an assertion. This is pre-repair #1054 evidence.
Initial old-code replay exposed the valid-marker refusal but also lacked a copied runner fixture. Two errors retained; later old-red-v2 provides more specific assertion evidence.
Formatting invocation could not import Black in the selected native environment. No formatting or validation success is inferred.
Original driver rejected actual source checkpoint0999 as Wrong actual MIM base; genuine #1054 checkpoint contract finding, later repaired through explicit baseline/checkpoint binding.
First invocation refused the supplied non-fresh/run-owned context output path before exercising the checkpoint check. The corrected v2 attempt separately proves #1054.

The git-NUL mutation triggered a real inventory ValueError, but the harness required an assertion-form failure and rejected its own result. Retained as mutation-harness failure, not a completed mutant suite.
Operator invocation pointed to output/does-not-exist. Python exited before test collection; subsequent native test runs are separately recorded.
Removing the native just-test final gate causes the explicit coverage-command assertion to fail. This verifies the continuation keeps native coverage gating.

Draft fixture read state from the native transaction result instead of the separately saved completed receipt. The log preserves KeyError state; corrected test reads the saved receipt. No production application was attempted.

Pytest cacheprovider failed internally on cache/lastfailed containment before completing tests. Later invocation disabled cacheprovider and default addopts; this run establishes no product defect or passing tests.

Synthetic raw KG fixture supplied kgm:fixture although the native builder adds kgm itself, yielding kgm:kgm:fixture and a row comparison failure. Corrected fixture input uses fixture; the actual producer contract was retained.
First generation invocation supplied a prior path that did not exist; prior.is_file assertion failed before generation. Subsequent actual generation receipts remain separate.

Initial mutation driver replaced PYTHONPATH and lost native Claw imports. Its baseline four tests and mutant one test were all skipped; the inner positive PASS label was false and is not accepted. Overall attempt failed. Repaired v2 preserves native PYTHONPATH and requires executed passes with zero skips; its results are separate.
Original generation harness failed two controls for distinct-prior/current-canonical input binding. #1055 repair and actual corrected generation are separately archived.

Combined native16fd and producer9bd test process hit the correct imported-module-origin guard. Isolated producer verification was separate; later maintained integration test repair is explicitly tracked by #1060.
Operator invocation pointed to output/does-not-exist. No package tests ran; later successful native package tests are separate.
Test helper import lacked the tests package qualifier and raised ModuleNotFoundError before promotion behavior. Corrected import uses tests.test_owned_name_policy.

Native bounded promotion guard correctly rejected a synthetic Glycerol_3-phosphate fixture/projection row mismatch. Fixture setup was corrected before subsequent runs; retained log does not establish the exact old label cell. No production promotion occurred in this attempt.

Negative fixture altered only source-receipt JSON whitespace, so its semantic receipt remained valid and the expected exception was absent. The control now changes approval to APPROVED to exercise meaningful refusal; no production guard was relaxed.

Strict native unchanged-cohort refresh correctly rejected the newly appended canonical policy metadata. #1057 was resolved through new independently authored metadata authority and fresh evidence, with strict refresh unchanged; original ten successful stages were preserved.

Pre-repair source-writer boundary tests failed to reject a newly reserved promotion artifact and symlink directory. #1051 original finding evidence; repaired guards and subsequent controls are separate.

Actual first focused gate stopped with one failed producer-import test and368 passes. Correct producer-origin refusal exposed the shared-process test defect; #1060 repair and forward-only context/seal migration retain the failure and all completed products.
Outer continuation stopped on the same failed focused gate tracked in #1060. Later QC/full-suite stages had not run in this execution; restarted gates use a separately reviewed forward context.
Second disposable durable-overlay replay lacked the diagnostic pair-plan input. No production mutation; exact missing input was added before successful independent native recapture.

Initial disposable durable-overlay replay correctly rejected an assembler input hash mismatch. No native verifier relaxation; exact transitive dependencies were supplied for the later successful recapture.

The unchanged native just test recipe completed its pytest phase but failed to spawn the coverage console entrypoint before required coverage reports; the outer controller stopped. Both original failed exits and receipts remain unchanged. The repaired-runtime unchanged just-test retry subsequently passed (receipt SHA256 44ef9dafbe2b63080a3c431c42d1ddd138a87ef5b13a5e110b744de7961f605d). Suffix completion ddbf514f438313770a8b06708c80c7d55853a5bf877e3552722cfab30fa63d55 binds the five prior successful gates, successful pre/post verification and the successful retry. Independent actual review a5566c46b809bad084120930f2ea49fa716db5d4098c1d09421dae3cdfc58199 confirmed that completion and the unchanged inputs/products. No original failed execution is relabeled or given a fabricated completion.

# Step 5 owned-name policy — execution evidence

The six required native gates have successful command receipts: focused regressions, full `just qc`, CURIE/product validation, unified rejection/freshness checks, writer audit and the unchanged full `just test` retry. Focused regressions passed 370 tests. The full native recipe passed 3,797 tests with one skip and 33 warnings in 846.48 seconds; maintained-package coverage was 72% (5,649 statements, 1,609 missed), exceeding the 35% gate, and the separate scripts report was 31%. The prior failed attempts remain explicitly preserved below.

This archive records the bounded consumer adoption of the merged Claw owned-name policy producer `9bd09b2ba163212a65289b91313f98cb0937476f`, using the existing native validation runtime `16fd7c9484d98b14a53aec55616d26dae70a0af7`. The MIM baseline is `be7170deb00a7c5490f8ade82facf86d45a852a4`. Actual source/generation checkpoint `0999ab53e2b20740db6249da0351a280bf3fb2ba` remains historical attribution; portable archive verification does not need that feature commit or the original machine paths.

The source receipt covers 13 owners: three actual YAML corrections and ten byte-identical owners with export-only changes. The canonical projection keeps 2,981 rows, changes 15 rows, and leaves the other 2,966 mapping decisions unchanged. Its scoped suppression sidecar has 11 pairs and the retained Rule K baseline has 23 deferred pairs. The generic diagnostic candidate has 2,974 rows and 25 suppression events covering 20 unique pairs. The diagnostic candidate is not the full canonical promotion policy. Receipt 19 records the bounded canonical change and preserves its 18 predecessors.

Native candidate acceptance is `PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS`: native invariant checks and schema validation succeeded, with Rule K evaluated against an empty in-memory baseline. B4 checked the available ontology transforms; BTO coverage for one row and MICRO coverage for 73 rows was unavailable under the native warn-and-skip contract. Missing coverage is not reported as a label match. Full scientific release remains `FAIL`, distinct from structural integrity and supported-subset validation. This work grants no new scientific approval.

The old automatic companion refresh correctly refused the new canonical policy metadata. Its strict comparator was retained. Independent review assessed the current metadata, all 51 claims and 20 cohort owners, the complete 2,680-path native ownership inventory and the scoped policy evidence. A new authority and fresh evidence preserve 50 `SUPPORTED` and one `WITHHOLD` disposition, including the prior scientific payloads and reasons. Native publication/export/validation then produced the new companion bundle. The actual review capture uses durable baseline `be7170deb00a7c5490f8ade82facf86d45a852a4`; the superseded truthful `0999` capture remains historical evidence only. Native consumers still require the declared durable base to be available; this archive does not waive that native contract.

The unified rebuild changes only two synonym cells. Its identity fields and the separately tracked raw-source identity concern remain outside this correction. ## Archive contract

`manifest.json` maps each original identity and raw SHA256 to a content-addressed payload. Multiple versions of an original path remain distinct. Equal bytes are stored once in `payloads.tar.gz`, or once as an exact already-compressed blob. The full 2,955 individual MIM record paths (2,680 mapped and 275 unmapped), selected producer/native code, historical/current decision tables and compact proof documents are preserved. Later source-YAML edits do not change these archived bytes.

Seven ontology databases are deliberately omitted, with exact historical hashes and captured native label responses retained. The exact hashes of 15,915 external CultureMech unified-source inputs and 46 large derived products are also retained as qualified omissions. This package verifies recorded provenance, comparisons and native outcomes; it does not claim standalone regeneration of the omitted databases, CultureMech corpus, browser products or large KGX/backlog outputs. Disposable Git checkouts, caches and mutant fixture trees are excluded.

`selection.final.json` is the explicit evidence selection. `final-inputs.json` binds that exact selection, its README and the verifier. The default verifier reads archived bytes rather than historical absolute paths or transient Git objects:

```sh
python reports/owned_name_policy_669_20261101/execution/verify.py verify \
  --package reports/owned_name_policy_669_20261101/execution
```

After commit, add `--repository . --require-tracked` to compare every package file with its current HEAD blob. This works after a squash and in a shallow consumer without the old feature objects. `--current-scope` is a separate optional check of selected current maintained paths; future legitimate curation can invalidate that check while historical archive verification continues to pass. A trusted committed package or externally pinned manifest is the integrity anchor; hashes alone are not independent scientific authority.

To inspect a selected original, locate its original path and SHA256 in `manifest.json`, then read the named SHA member from `payloads.tar.gz` or the exact blob path. The selection's graph bindings distinguish recorded-only omissions from archived original bytes.

The final whole-change native review, committed-head/body review and subsequent CI/queue/merge attestations follow package freeze and remain external or in later immutable supplements. Their absence from this archive avoids a circular hash dependency and is not a claim that they have completed.
